What you send and how it is sent
Workarounds for games that need them
For games that wrap their lines and cannot be told not to: the lines are joined again, so triggers see them whole and the text fits your screen. Experimental.

Game data for scripts, such as your health and the room you are in.

The game\'s description of itself, such as its name and how many are playing.
Sounds and music the game asks to play.

Tells the game what Mudlet can show, such as colours, and whether you use a screen reader.
Tells the game about Mudlet in more detail than MTTS, for games that ask.
Tells the game how many columns and rows of text fit, so it can lay out its text to fit.
Lets the game and Mudlet agree on the text encoding, such as UTF-8.
Tells the game about Mudlet, for games that ask, as MNES does.
Declines the game\'s offer to compress what it sends, for games where that garbles the text.
For games that send it where it does not belong, which breaks lines or prompts apart.
Fix unnecessary linebreaks on GA servers
Some games, such as Achaea, send a line break too many after each prompt. Mudlet turns this on for the games it knows need it.
line breaks, newline, prompt, go ahead, IRE, Iron Realms
Send Mudlet\'s version with its name
Some games expect a version number when they ask which client you use, though the telnet standard does not allow one there.
TTYPE, terminal type, MTTS, client, version
Read MXP the game does not offer
For games that send MXP links and menus without offering MXP first. To have no MXP at all, turn MXP off on the Connection page.
Prepare trigger variables as scripts read them
Makes triggers faster; scripts see the same values. Turn it off only if a script or package goes through Lua\'s globals with pairs on _G and misbehaves.
performance, speed, faster, matches, multimatches, Lua
Show script errors in the game\'s text
So you can see why a script or package is not working.
Lua, error, debug, bug, broken, package
Certificates, and what the game may install or play
Let the game install its packages
Some games send their own interface or scripts over GMCP, which Mudlet installs.
Let the game play sounds and music
The sounds and music a game sends over GMCP, which Mudlet downloads. Needs GMCP on the Connection page.
Connects securely to a game whose certificate has run out. Someone could pretend to be the game.
TLS, SSL, secure, encryption, certificate, error
Connects securely to a game that signed its own certificate. Someone could pretend to be the game.
The connection is still encrypted, but nothing checks that it goes to the game. Use only if you must.
Text size, colours and the map
The app\'s screens take their colours from your wallpaper. Off, they use Mudlet\'s own. The game\'s text keeps the game\'s colours.
Tell games you use a screen reader?
Games that ask are told, and some then send text laid out for screen readers. You can change this in the settings.
